records.note: Highest load-excited V-regression resistance proxy (vreg_R_pack_mohm) among the 121 of 294 ens-clean proxy drives passing an excitation/support gate (n_vreg_samples ≥ 741, peak-current p95 ≥ 52 A). Holder: pack mean 16.0°C, SoC mean 67.8%, I_p95 54.5 A, 1260 regression samples, 23.1 km, V-sag cross-check 172.1 mΩ. Gated median 125.7 mΩ; holder residual after linear pack-T control = +2.4 SD (fitted dR/dT = -2.62 mΩ/°C; T-adjusted to 34.4°C the highest is Aug30 D7 at 149.2 mΩ). Selection effect, as an IID residual-model reference distribution (fitted T model + residuals resampled independently across the gated drives, pooled and homoscedastic with the regression support n_vreg_samples ignored, the pool and the fitted T model including the holder's own drive, B=4000; not a day-clustered interval for the observed maximum and not a noise test): the same 121 drives and temperature mix give a reference maximum of 173.9 mΩ (central 95% range of the reference maxima 163.2–189.1); the holder sits at percentile 99 of that distribution. Day dependence is not modelled: the 121 gated drives fall on 60 calendar days. A maximum over noisy per-drive estimates is biased upward by selection, so the holder value is a selection-biased extreme of noisy per-drive proxy estimates and is not interpreted as pack resistance, DCIR or SOH. Gate sensitivity of the holder: loose gate (n≥456, 223 drives) → Nov01 D1; primary gate (n≥741, I_p95≥52 A, 121 drives) → Nov06 D3; strict gate (n≥1274, I_p95≥58.3 A, 54 drives) → Oct08 D3 (holder changes with the gate — treat the identity as unstable). For contrast the UNGATED maximum (294 drives) is 250.9 mΩ on Oct03 D4 with only 367 regression samples. Gates were placed at the observed dispersion elbow of the proxy (T-controlled residual SD 18.3 mΩ below n_vreg_samples=456, 10.5 above), not at a physical threshold. Load-excited in-drive proxy, V and I on separate polling timestamps: NOT an SOH, DCIR or capacity measurement.

cellHealthTrend.methodNote: Bootstrap OLS/Huber on the pre-deconfounded cell_spread_loaded_p95_adj_mv series (day-cluster bootstrap CI), methodologically distinct from the authoritative single-stage cluster-robust-OLS estimator on the raw series with pack-temperature and peak-current as explicit controls. The two can disagree on whether the interval spans zero; that is expected, not an error, and the authoritative object governs headline claims.
cellHealthTrend.huberSlopeCiMethod: Two-stage day-clustered percentile bootstrap (4000 draws, seed 42, 126 days): per draw the first-stage Huber fit, I_ref and the adjusted values are recomputed before the second-stage Huber slope. Calibrated in simulation; non-authoritative.

caveats: EV state is eng_rpm <= 400 (engine not rotating), the same threshold engine_on_pct uses. The M46/M48 motored-unfuelled state counts here as engine ON (it is not engine-off by RPM), so these figures are a conservative reading of "electric"; the comparison with a zero-logged-fuel definition on the fuel-instrumented drives is evTraction.zeroFuelVariant.

The +/-3 s nearest-sample channel alignment and the symmetric 3 s state debounce can move the engine-off boundaries in either direction (an engine-on run shorter than 3 s inside an engine-off run is absorbed, which raises the EV share; an engine-off run shorter than 3 s inside an engine-on run is absorbed, which lowers it): every EV distance and time figure is an estimated RPM-defined engine-off share, not a one-sided bound. Detector settings (threshold, sample age, debounce, alignment) give a sensitivity range, not a confidence interval; unknown RPM is never counted as engine-off (M427, audit F04).
Runs at the top of the distribution recover 30-50% of throughput as regen mid-run, so the observed maximum is not a buffer-drain range; runMaxUnassistedKm is.

M62: the census rests on nValid of nDrives (supportPct); the balance is channel-gated. Drives whose ensemble outlier flags were never fitted (NaN) are treated as non-outliers and INCLUDED -- see nUnflaggedIncluded / kmUnflaggedIncluded for how much distance that assumption admits.
The barometric PID is 1 kPa (~83 m) quantised and cannot resolve run-scale gradient, so no terrain attribution is made for long runs.

detectorSensitivity.label: raw/ = sha256-verified originals (M366); detector-sensitivity range over declared conventions; not a confidence interval; model-derived
detectorSensitivity.reading: Range of the engine-off distance share over declared detector conventions (RPM threshold, RPM alignment tolerance and direction, debounce), each recomputed on the same drives with speed, odometer scale and distance denominator held fixed. The detector effect is the paired difference on the drives valid under both settings; support lost / gained is reported separately. The range is deterministic given the data: it is not a confidence interval and not a bound on the true share. The sampling interval of the released share is the day-clustered percentile interval below. Stress rows are shown beside the range and never enter it.

comparability.rule: at least 90 % of the released drives and at least 90 % of the released distance remain valid under the variant

factorial.design: RPM threshold x alignment (nearest / backward / forward at matched width) x tolerance x debounce, core values only

evaluatedOn.noResult: the drive without a result has zero logged distance in the master

zeroFuelVariant.label: zero-logged-fuel versus RPM-defined engine-off distance share (logged / app-calculated fuel rate); descriptive; no physical claim
zeroFuelVariant.reading: Share of the logged distance with a zero logged fuel rate, set beside the RPM-defined engine-off share on the SAME drives (those that carry the logged, app-calculated fuel-rate channel; this population is not the one of the released engine-off share, so the two levels are never mixed). Four states per second: A engine off and no fuel, B engine turning and no fuel, C engine off and fuel logged (an inconsistency flag), D fuelled. Day-clustered 95 % intervals; sensitivities are ranges over declared conventions, never combined with the interval. Descriptive: no physical claim about injection or the controller.

metricConvention.note: Counts are throughput integrated from logged current (estimated, offset-uncorrected) divided by the rated capacity 5 Ah (Nissan Article-10, documentary; not a measurement and not a confirmation of the fitted SoC scale). GTC is a local double-counting convention, not a recognised metric. FCE is the quantity that corresponds to the standard equivalent-full-cycle (EFC) definition; the residual gap from 1.000 is charge-discharge imbalance (SoC drift, unlogged use, residual-balance offset, auxiliaries), not a definitional difference. Every figure here scales inversely with the reference; physical throughput is unchanged.

energyPath.basis: M63. Corpus-level pack-terminal energy accounting over the ens_outlier_v2-clean drives carrying the BMS current channel. The operating-state charge partition is the M12 torque-verified four-way partition and is exhaustive by construction.

chargeSources.label: Engine-on / non-braking charge

chargeSources.label: Engine-on / braking overlap
chargeSources.detail: engine ON while the motor brakes — mixed operating state; the physical split between generator output and recovered braking energy is unidentified

chargeSources.label: Engine-off / braking charge

chargeSources.detail: engine OFF, motor not braking — unattributed by the -15 N·m threshold; not a metered motor or generator source

regimeTransition.method: First-order Markov transition matrix over the drive-type regime taxonomy, chronological drive-to-drive. Cells with 1<=count<5 suppressed (stability flag, still counted in row denominator). Unknown-type drives break the chain.

permutationTest.verdict: Day-structure-preserving null rejected at p<0.05: the observed transition matrix departs from what within-day label reshuffling produces.

secondOrder.verdict: Second-order model does NOT improve BIC over first-order -- the extra memory depth is not supported by the data at this sample size, reported as a null result.

heldOutLogLik.method: Leave-one-day-out: fit the first-order count matrix on all other days (Jeffreys-smoothed, alpha=0.5, so a held-out day is never scored against a hard-zero cell), score the held-out day's own transitions under it, sum across all days. A genuine out-of-sample prediction score, not an in-sample fit statistic.

carryoverLink.note: Explicit link to interDriveCarryover (M223.1): both share the SAME consecutive-chronological-pair construction (_full_datetimes) and the SAME parking-gap bins (reused verbatim here as conditionalTransitions.byParkingGapBin). interDriveCarryover characterizes the thermal/SoC state each gap leaves behind; byParkingGapBin here characterizes how that SAME gap relates to which regime the next drive turns out to be.

regimeTransition.hardeningMethod: M223.2 (P1.5, enhancement plan): statistical hardening layer over regimeTransition's (M142) first-order countMatrix -- Jeffreys-Dirichlet + day-clustered-bootstrap per-cell uncertainty, independence-residual heatmap, a day-block-preserving label-permutation test (seed=42, 4000 draws), a second-order (previous-two-drive-type) model with BIC/likelihood-ratio comparison against a first-order re-fit on the identical triples sample, transitions conditioned on parking-gap bin / time-of-day / weekday (the SAME gap bins interDriveCarryover/M223.1 uses), leave-one-day-out predictive log-likelihood, row-wise Shannon entropy and expected run length, and an explicit link back to interDriveCarryover. regimeTransition's own pre-existing fields (countMatrix, cells, stationary, persistence, sessionVariants, etc.) are computed by _regime_transition, UNCHANGED by this function.

seasonalLife.basis: M28 model-based all-year extrapolation (the cold tail below the lowest logged pack-probe reading is modelled, not observed; assumption-driven, superseded by real winter logs)

selectedConstant.basis: constant all-season selectedConstantMix carried through the M28 seasonal throughput model -> carries climatic stress; measured:false (inherits the seasonal assumption load). observedConstant.basis: constant all-season OBSERVED logged distance mix carried through the M28 seasonal throughput model -> carries climatic stress; measured:false (the workload input is measured, but the seasonal throughput multiplier and monthly mix-shift are still M28 assumptions, same as selectedConstant). packThermalMeasured.driveTimeShareGeCMeaning: Share of drive time (duration-weighted) spent in drives whose drive-average pack temperature (T_pack_mean_avg) is at or above the threshold; a drive-average estimand. It is not the share of logged samples above the threshold; the sample-resolved occupancy is a separate quantity (M637/M638, self-audit W1-08, owner decision D-03).

sampleOccupancy.rule: 2 s midpoint grid; supported when at least 3 of the 4 pack probe channels ([BMS] HV Battery Temperature Sensor 1 (℃); [BMS] HV Battery Temperature Sensor 2 (℃); [BMS] HV Battery Temperature Sensor 3 (℃); [BMS] HV Battery Temperature Sensor 4 (℃)) hold a reading no older than 45 s (sample and hold); pack temperature = mean of the available probes; a reading equal to the threshold counts as at or above it; pooled ratio of sums over canonical-clean drives
sampleOccupancy.meaning: Share of logged drive time (supported seconds) with a mean pack-probe reading at or above the threshold (sample-resolved). Logged BMS sensor readings (an occupancy of logged readings, not an exposure measurement). A different estimand from driveTimeShareGeC (share of drive time in drives whose drive-average pack temperature is at or above the threshold), which carries no interval. Read the two side by side; neither stands alone as a hot-tail figure (M638, self-audit W1-08, owner decision D-03).

hotTail.note: Logged-sensor high-T cycle-damage sensitivity (the logged corpus is almost entirely Warm and Shoulder ambient class (Cold-class drives are thinly observed and concentrated, see cohortSupport), so pack thermal exposure is characterised directly for that range). Reported as a labelled sensitivity only, never folded into the primary crossing. Calendar-aging axis (calendarLifeYrShaded) is duty-blended/parked-dominated and is NOT affected by this in-drive cycling term.

assumptions._provenance: M28 (2026-07-10). Inputs for the all-year seasonal cycle-life extrapolation. monthlyTempC = user-supplied Kyiv monthly mean daily temperatures (external climatology; NOT measured by this study; note it diverges by up to 1.1C from the older archived 'climate' block, which is retained unchanged per provenance convention). All model parameters below are assumptions carried with lo/mid/hi bands because the cold tail below the lowest logged pack-probe reading is modelled, not observed; consumptionSlopePerC is anchored to the 15-30% hybrid winter consumption penalty range reported in cold-climate fleet literature, coldSoakRetention encodes inter-drive pack cooling under the 5-6 short-city-drives/day working pattern, and platingDamageWeights are generic NMC low-temperature stress multipliers (sensitivity only, not fitted to this pack).

hotTail._provenance: M85 (2026-08-05): high-temperature cycle-damage sensitivity, symmetric to the cold platingDamageWeights. Unlike the cold tail, this one comes from logged BMS sensor readings: the logged corpus is almost entirely Warm and Shoulder ambient class (Cold-class drives are thinly observed and concentrated, see cohortSupport), so pack thermal exposure is characterised directly for that range (at M85, 2026-08-05 corpus, historical: time-weighted mean pack ~34.2C, 54.3% of drive-time >=35C, highway thermal rise +17C above ambient; the live values are in hotTail.packThermalMeasured). A hot class-month is one whose modeled pack temp (ambient + logged per-class rise) exceeds tempThresholdC; its cycles are damage-weighted either by the per-temp Arrhenius factor (arrhenius block, Ea/refC) or by the flatDamageWeights ladder. Reported as a labelled sensitivity only, never folded into the primary crossing (same discipline as plating). This is a CYCLE-damage overlay; the calendar-aging axis (calendarLifeYrShaded) is duty-blended and dominated by the parked/winter state, so it is NOT changed by this term.
hotTail.note: High-T stress is the in-drive cycling accelerant (pack does its charge/discharge work at ~35C, ~1.95x calendar-basis Arrhenius acceleration vs 25C). It is distinct from and opposite to the cold plating tail; both are carried so the two ends of the temperature axis are visible.

assumptions._mixProvenanceM85: M85 (2026-08-05): scenario mixes reconciled to a highway-dominant forward-usage frame, consistent with the observed logged distance mix (67.6% highway at M85, 2026-08-05 corpus, historical; the live distance mix is in observedMix). Selected blend is now the CONSTANT all-season selectedConstantMix (city0.40/mixed0.10/highway0.50, == the cold/working-season endpoint), run through the seasonal throughput model so it CARRIES climatic stress (it is no longer a pure warm-season floor -> measured:false). All-Year season-switches between warmSeasonMix (holiday, city0.20/mixed0.10/highway0.70) and workSeasonMix (working, == selectedConstantMix). highwayShareRelReduction zeroed: the seasonal city/highway split is now explicit in the two mixes, so the old -10% relative highway shift would double-count. Prior M28 city-dominant mixes (work 0.70/0.20/0.10, warm 0.55/0.30/0.15) superseded here.
assumptions.kmDistribution: uniform-monthly (odometer-average annualKm already spans a full real year incl. one winter; no extra seasonal km re-weighting imposed)

arrhenius.note: Ea=0.5eV reproduces the archived climate block's Jan 0.14x factor; refCalendarLifeYr=15 is the generic NMC 25C-reference calendar estimate the archived 27-35yr band was scaled from.

In the reference draw, emulated slow-cadence thinning (each column thinned independently, which also alters the I-V co-timing; not attributed to sampling density) lowers the proxy by 1.6-1.8 mΩ on the 78 fast-regime drives that keep a proxy and removes it from 29 of 107 fast-regime drives; across 41 slow-pool configurations (11 coupled draws and seeds, M532; 30 single-factor and pool-size runs of 20, 40 or 80 slow drives, M534) the era-mean lowering spans 0.9-2.3 mΩ (fast1) and 0.8-3.6 mΩ (fast2) (min / max across configurations, descriptive, not an interval), the paired interval includes zero in 8 of 82 era configurations (fast1 4, fast2 4), and the spread cannot be apportioned between the pool draw and the seeds (standard-deviation ratio 1.4 and 0.9, not resolved at 10 replicates per arm), computed on the previous basis (274 clean drives) (emulated sampling sensitivity, not a causal cadence effect; M393 study on 274 clean drives, stale: the clean-drive count is now 294).

power.relevance: For a series-hybrid power buffer cycled at 20-33 C peaks and ~4 % mean DoD, resistance rise is the more plausible functional limit than Ah loss; it is also the only one of the two this dataset can observe.

fadeModes.coupling: The 20,000-GTC convention implicitly bundles both mechanisms into one throughput budget. They are reported separately here because their evidence status differs by kind, not by degree: one is entirely modeled, the other is measured and currently null.

officialDisclosureCorrelation.basis: M79 (2026-07-31). Cross-check of the Nissan X-Trail e-POWER (T33) Article 10 (Regulation (EU) 2023/1542) battery durability disclosure against this study's own measured / modeled figures. Source disclosure and supplier identity are external reference content (cfg.officialDisclosure / cfg.batterySupplier); every comparison figure on this side is pipeline-computed from the live drive_master.csv + config, so the whole block recomputes as the corpus grows.

official._provenance: M79 (2026-07-31). External regulatory disclosure, NOT measured by this study. Nissan X-Trail e-POWER (T33) battery performance and durability table, filed under Article 10, Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 (the EU Batteries Regulation). official.note: Capacity fade / power fade / internal-resistance increase are all defined AT the 14yr / 190,000km condition, not as a linear rate; this study's officialDisclosureCorrelation.resistance.trendContext uses a linear-in-throughput approximation only to sanity-check whether the estimated M25 proxy null result is consistent with the disclosed life-point figure at the CURRENT mileage, not to restate the disclosure as a rate.

supplier._provenance: M79 (2026-07-31). Vehicle Energy Japan (VE-J) news release, 2023-09-19 -- 2023 Nissan Global Supplier Award, Global Innovation Award, for battery cells/modules supplying the Nissan X-Trail e-POWER system.
supplier.awardName: 2023 Nissan Global Supplier Award -- Global Innovation Award
supplier.productDescription: Lithium-ion battery cells and modules; the award citation names high output, safety, and long life as the optimal technology solution for the X-Trail e-POWER system, i.e. a power-optimised cell design, not an energy-optimised one.
supplier.note: Neither Nissan nor VE-J material reviewed publishes cathode chemistry/stoichiometry. chemistry.note: Series-cell count and cell-voltage window are a raw-file spot-check inference (pack-voltage extremum over the full master vs. observed max single-cell voltage on the subset of files exposing full cell telemetry), NOT a full-corpus raw scan and NOT a manufacturer-published series count -- the OBD PID set exposes only cell channels #01-#80 regardless of the true series count. The window EXCLUDES LFP and is CONSISTENT WITH a layered-oxide (NMC/NCA-class) cathode; operational voltage/current behaviour cannot uniquely identify the cathode, so this is NOT an NMC identification. OEM material discloses only lithium-ion. Pack voltage range IS a full-corpus, pipeline-computed figure (V_pack_median extrema).

power.note: Single-sample peak battery discharge (73.3 kW, Jun19 D1; a reconstructed I x V sample) exceeds the 66.0 kW figure, which the OEM material discloses at 80 % SoC; no pulse duration is stated, so the two are not directly comparable, and this study does not explain the exceedance. The nearest logged Sensor-1 probe reading was 39 C, co-timed (within 1 s): the T1 sample is 0.167 s after the peak sample. The motor's rated output (150 kW) exceeds the disclosed battery figure by 84.0 kW (difference of rated figures, losses not included); the split of such demand between battery and generator cannot be resolved from the BMS shunt alone (see energyPath).

resistance.note: NOT a like-for-like comparison. The official figure is a standardized long-pulse DCIR at 80% SoC, ~25°C. our vsag_R / vreg_R are instantaneous, load-excited in-drive proxies (ohmic + fast polarization only) at ~64% SoC on a warm pack -- a different resistance definition, not a degraded-vs-new state. The ratio between the two levels must NEVER be read as a state-of-health percentage. What IS comparable is the estimated TREND (see powerFade / fadeModes.power), which is the null result reported separately below.

trendContext.note: Linear-in-throughput approximation ONLY, for sanity-checking the null result -- not a fitted degradation law. At the current mileage fraction of the official 190,000 km life point (25.1%), the disclosed lifetime IR rise implies an expected-so-far increase (~18.8%) at or below this window's own CI half-width (±28.2% over 2.26yr) -- i.e. the M25 interval does not exclude the official trajectory at this mileage (a consistency check, not a validation).

officialDisclosureCorrelation.verdictHeadline: No official figure contradicts a study finding. The disclosure's own structure -- large tolerated capacity fade alongside separately tracked power fade and a large internal-resistance increase, on a high power/energy-ratio pack -- independently corroborates this study's central framing: the HV battery is a power buffer, and internal-resistance-driven power fade, not capacity fade, is the functionally meaningful degradation mode. The one figure that must never be read as a direct level match is internal resistance (see resistance.note) -- track its TREND against ours, never its absolute value.
officialDisclosureCorrelation.note: No warranty implication can be derived from any information here, per the source disclosure's own disclaimer. Figures transcribed from the manufacturer's published compliance table; this study did not independently verify the disclosure's own test protocol.

dodSocLevelSensitivity.basis: M91. Diagnostic SoC-window-level split of the existing rf_damage_k2 (M17) total, re-blended through a labeled, unverified weight ladder cross-checked against Wikner (Chalmers, 2017). Never folds into rf_damage_k2 itself or any GTC/FCE crossing.
dodSocLevelSensitivity.note: At the corpus's observed band split, the weight ladder collapses to an almost class-blind multiplier on w_hi (essentially all classes already sit in the >= 50% band) -- the scenario-level ratioVsFlat and the class ranking are correspondingly close to flat. That is the finding: shallow DEPTH is protective (unchanged from rf_damage_k2/M17); shallow SoC-window LEVEL is not, because this buffer's operating window sits almost entirely above socLevelHiPct.

kLadderScenarios.basis: k-exponent (Woehler/S-N) sensitivity ladder on the M17 rainflow damage proxy. rf_damage_k = sum(count*(range/100)^k) over the same ens_outlier_v2-clean, SoC-eligible corpus and floor (RF_FLOOR_PCT) as M17 (n=661). m(k)=sum(rf_efc)/sum(rf_damage_k); rf_efc == rf_damage at k=1, so m(1)=1.0 and the k=1 rung IS the flat GTC convention. Implied life = fadeModes flat crossing at the reference GTC threshold * m(k), assuming forward DoD-shape ~ observed.
kLadderScenarios.note: m(k) grows near-exponentially because the duty is shallow-dominated: each unit rise in k discounts a 2%-DoD cycle ~50x while leaving a full-DoD cycle unchanged. Across the physically admissible NMC range k=1.0..2.5 the mitigation spans about 1x..29x; k=3.0 is a flagged aggressive extreme. Implied lives of hundreds of years at k>=2.5 are NOT predictions: they exceed the calendar-aging ceiling by an order of magnitude, so real end-of-life is set by calendar aging and the still-uncaptured winter-driving risk, not by cycling. The ladder shows the LEVERAGE of the unvalidated exponent; the flat k=1 GTC convention remains the planning anchor.
kLadderScenarios._provenance: Diagnostic sensitivity only. k is NMC-generic, NOT derived from this pack. Nothing here is folded into rf_damage_k2, cycleLife, or any fadeModes GTC/FCE crossing. Read WITH M17 (shallow DEPTH protective, unchanged) and the winter-gap caveat. Replaces the retired M91 SoC-level weight-ladder chart; M91 band-share (Panel A) + dodSocLevelSensitivity retained.
kLadderScenarios._retracted: M113 (audit P0-01): implied-cycle-life outputs (scenarios[].byK[].yr, scenarios[].flatCrossingYr, plausibilityCeilingYr) retracted as dimensionally invalid life conversions. Dimensionless relative damage m(k) = rungs[].mitigation is retained as the exposure quantity.

bufferImpulse.methodology: Engine-start events (RPM crosses from sustained-OFF to running within one ~1.3s sample) are the power-ramp interval; battery discharge current (M11 sign-flipped to discharge-positive) in excess of the local pre-restart baseline is integrated over the first contiguous above-threshold run following the crossing. Baseline is local to each restart and can be negative (net charging) in stop-start driving following a prior cycle's recharge tail -- a real driving-pattern feature, not an artefact. An unusually large single-event figure can partly reflect a coincident driver-demand transition (e.g. braking into the restart) rather than engine-lag buffering alone; median/p95, not max, are the headline figures for this reason.

rampLatency.methodology: Engine-start events (same RPM sustained-off -> running trigger as M116) are segmented into discrete RPM plateaus (250 rpm bins, >=3s minimum dwell), matching the load-point quantization already established by the M41 finding: the generator steps between a handful of operating points rather than holding a continuously variable RPM. Ramp latency is the time from the trigger to the first qualifying plateau; RPM is sampled at native ~1.3s intervals (async polled PID), and the mechanical ramp can complete within a single sample step -- a 0.0s reported latency means the ramp finished at or below telemetry resolution, not that it was instantaneous. Transition speed is vehicle speed in a +-2s window around each plateau-to-plateau boundary within the same engine-on cycle. This detector has no current-based eligibility gate (unlike M116), so its event count is not directly comparable to the buffer-impulse count.

latencyHistPos.note: nZero is the exactly-0.0s resolution-floor population (ramp completed within one telemetry sample); the histogram covers only latencies > 0 s.

startEventReconcile.methodology: Both detectors share ONE trigger definition (RPM sustained-off -> running); their event sets are subsets of that trigger population, differing only by downstream eligibility. M116 requires a battery discharge excess >=3A over the pre-restart baseline (current gate); M118 requires >=1 RPM plateau lasting >=3s (dwell gate). A trigger can pass one gate, both, or neither -- e.g. a brief restart with a current spike but no sustained plateau is buffer-only; a long low-current idle-up is ramp-only. This block makes the 2224-vs-3754 count difference explicit rather than leaving it as two unrelated headline numbers.

socHysteresis.methodology: Per-second state classification (1 Hz resampled grid, engine-on = rpm>500) across the corpus, distinct from the per-event M116/M118 detectors. Every second the engine is off is an at-risk sample for a start in the following second; every second it is on is at-risk for a stop. Marginal probability is tabulated by 5-point SoC bin; stratified probability adds a speed band (stationary <5, low 5-60, high >=60 km/h -- an independently-defined threshold for this per-second analysis only, NOT the same >=90 km/h boundary used by the drive_type Highway classifier (M115); the two serve different purposes and are not interchangeable). Both tables are filtered to cells with n>=30 to avoid presenting noisy small-sample estimates (e.g. a single-digit-n bin at the tails of the SoC range) with the same apparent weight as a well-supported one. Temperature and a recent-demand covariate were scoped out of this pass -- a full 4-way stratification fragments the sample too far for binned tables to remain trustworthy; that needs a regression-style model, not this pass. Replaces the dashboard's fixed per-class SoC hysteresis box with an actual probability surface: at matched SoC, P(start) differs by roughly two orders of magnitude between stationary and highway speed, showing SoC alone does not set the trigger point once demand is accounted for.

socHysteresisV2.methodology: M119-v2 (M147): two SEPARATE 1 Hz discrete-time hazard models -- a START model on engine-off seconds and a STOP model on engine-on seconds -- each predicting a canonical debounced transition in the following second. Five strictly-lagged predictors: SoC (age<=5s), validated speed (VCM/OBD priority, age<=2s), pack temperature (mean of >=3 of T1-T4, age<=15s), recent demand (START: median battery discharge kW over [t-8,t-2]; STOP: median max(target-torque,0) x speed demand INDEX over [t-5,t-1]) and log1p(state duration). Complementary-log-log link (discrete-time hazard); unpenalized fixed-basis GLM with restricted-cubic-spline smooths f1..f5 and low-degree cross-product interaction terms (not penalized -- no fit_regularized call, no penalty matrix, no smoothing-parameter selection anywhere in the fitting code) SoC x demand, T x demand, SoC x duration. Random-effects disclosure: a full crossed day x drive binomial GAMM is not tractable on the Python stack; the additive smooths and interactions are fit exactly, day/drive dependence is carried by day-clustered robust covariance for inference and by whole-day GROUPED CONTIGUOUS DAY-BLOCK k-fold cross-validation (each fold trains on all other blocks, including later-dated ones -- a leakage guard against same-day pseudo-replication, not a forward-only / rolling-origin split) for every reported generalization metric (the operative guard against treating seconds as independent); a separate forward-chaining rolling-origin validation is reported under sensitivity.rollingOrigin. The four-model ladder (SoC only -> +speed -> four-variable -> full five-variable duration-aware) improves monotonically on Brier, log loss and PR-AUC for both models, with day-clustered bootstrap CIs on the five-variable vs SoC-only PR-AUC that do not overlap -- SoC alone is a weak trigger predictor once speed, demand, temperature and state duration are known. Mechanistic sensitivity variables (SoC change since last transition, accumulated charge since start, engine coolant temperature, time since key-on) were tested but are not part of the primary five; only engine-coolant temperature gives a non-negligible out-of-sample improvement, and for the STOP model only.
socHysteresisV2.disclaimer: A five-variable, duration-aware observational model of engine start/stop probability conditional on SoC, speed, pack temperature, recent demand and elapsed engine-state duration -- not a reconstruction of Nissan’s proprietary ECU algorithm.

startDetectorBoundaryAudit.note: M231 (audit F05): detect_transitions() previously assumed the engine OFF at the grid origin and let any confirmed running run flip the state machine regardless of whether the documented >= 3s prior-OFF rule was actually observed, or whether the OFF label was only being held across an unresolved data gap. These are now explicit, non-exclusive diagnostic categories over the 6436 raw confirmed starts in this corpus: atGridOrigin (a strict subset of noPriorConfirmedOff -- no data exists before the recording began), noPriorConfirmedOff (the >=3s prior-off rule was never actually satisfied by an observed run -- excluded from START model training as an unverifiable label, not relabeled as a negative), and afterUnknownGap (the prior OFF confirmation is genuine, but an unobserved intermediate stop/start inside the immediately-preceding data gap cannot be ruled out -- retained as a confirmed positive with this timing caveat disclosed).

socHysteresisV2.recomputeBlockedReason: OOM-kill risk in this <=4GB-RAM environment (M148); recompute only on explicit user demand, see recomputePolicy.
socHysteresisV2.recomputePolicy: M119-v2 recomputation is opt-in by design: it is performed ONLY when explicitly requested by the user for a given session (recompute_m119v2=True / --recompute-m119v2) -- never automatically, never merely because the corpus has grown. Prior to M216 this was ALSO enforced by a reproducible OOM kill during run_ladder's fit sequence in this environment's <=4GB-RAM sandbox (M148: build_m119v2() alone, no other array computation in the process, reliably exhausted memory). M216 (2026-09-03) added explicit memory hygiene to m119v2_model.py (gc.collect() + del at every fold/candidate/model boundary in oos_predict/sensitivity_screen/run_ladder/_corpus_tables) which bounds peak RSS to <2GB even at the 320-drive corpus of the M216 verification -- verified by a successful full recompute (peak RSS 1874MB, 0B swap consumed of a 4GB session-scoped swapfile added as a precaution but not actually needed). The OOM is therefore no longer an unconditional blocker, but the opt-in gate is UNCHANGED: a full recompute is a single-core, ~11-12 minute operation and remains something to run only on explicit demand, not on every routine ingestion. Absent that explicit request, the last-fit block is carried forward unchanged and stamped frozenBasis=true.
socHysteresisV2.rollingOriginCvPolicy: M222.1 (enhancement plan): rolling-origin (forward-chaining) CV of the already-selected five-variable duration-aware spec, reported alongside (never replacing) the existing blocked-day CV. Independent of the recompute_m119v2 gate -- this can run and attach to an otherwise carried-forward socHysteresisV2 block without refitting the model itself. Opt-in by the same cadence convention as M119-v2 proper: carries forward unless recompute_rolling_origin_cv=True is passed explicitly, or no prior value exists yet.

detectorReconciliation.methodology: socHysteresisV2.nStartEvents/nStopEvents count CONFIRMED transitions from detect_transitions() (m119v2_model.py): a sustained >=3s off interval followed by a sustained >=2s CONFIRMED running interval (run-based debounce on BOTH sides). startEventChain.attritionFunnel.nTrig (compute_summary_arrays._engine_start_triggers, shared by bufferImpulse/M116, rampLatency/M118, handoffSequence/M147, this milestone's startEventChain/M221) fires on a single RPM>800 sample preceded by a sustained >=3s off period, with NO confirmation requirement on the following high-RPM reading -- a momentary blip above 800 rpm immediately followed by a drop back down still counts as a trigger there, but not as a confirmed start here. The two detectors are therefore EXPECTED to diverge (model count below trigger count), by construction, not by data-quality accident; this field states the divergence rather than leaving it implicit or reconciling it away.

headroomUtilization.methodology: Logged [BMS] Input/Output possible power, the limit the BMS reports (logged / app-calculated): the (kW) pair since 2026-09-30 and the (hp) pair before it, converted with the metric horsepower factor 0.735499 (the former mechanical factor 0.7457 put every limit 1.4 % too high); files are selected by header, not by date. Utilisation = logged I x V power (charge-positive raw, M11) aligned to the nearest possible-power sample within 2s (merge_asof nearest) divided by the BMS-reported limit; it is not a physical capability. Coverage: 432 of 665 corpus drives carry the channel (429 analysed). The channel is polled far less densely than ordinary BMS current / voltage (median gap per era in coverage.byEra), so a few utilisation values exceed 1.0, most plausibly a stale match during fast current transients; not clipped. The reported limit may be saturated at 63.75 kW (255 x 0.25 kW): 89614 of 100018 possible-power samples are at or above 63.7 kW (ceiling.byEra); this is not identified, and the statistics are also given for events with the limit below it (conditional on the denominator, not a censoring correction). Median and 95th percentile carry a day-clustered percentile bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws); maximum and nAbove1 are descriptive. Eras are reported side by side; no contrast between them is drawn, and nothing here shows that the limit constrained driving. Single vehicle / ~single driver.
