recordsContract: Every record carries a `disclosure` object: the eligibility/sanity rule, the count excluded by that rule (excludedByCap), and — when any were excluded — the raw pre-cap extremum (records_disclosure.py, audit B8). No extremum is reported without disclosing what its rule removed. M295: every record also states whether its winning drive is canonically clean (winnerValidity); a canonically invalid drive cannot win (builder eligibility), and conceptually weak extrema are flagged auditOnly.

regenCaptureV2.label: raw/ = sha256-verified originals (M366); apparent battery-side KE recovery with assumed masses (observed, not SOC-standardized); interval-based extractor v2; not a correction of the legacy values
regenCaptureV2.reading: Ratio of sums of battery-side charge energy to kinetic energy lost over the same engine-off deceleration intervals (consecutive native speed samples, actual duration, current and voltage interpolated, unknown RPM never engine-off). Cells are observed, not standardized for SOC: temperature and SOC are confounded in the logged data. Intervals are counted in every speed bin they touch; support counts strict-drop intervals. A cell is 'supported' with at least 200 strict-drop intervals on at least 10 drives and 5 days, otherwise 'thin' (exploratory). The assumed-mass range is kept apart from the statistical interval. The 300 rpm engine-off proxy, the assumed masses and the cadence regime are declared conventions; a nonzero legacy-versus-v2 difference is not a correction of the legacy values.
regenCaptureV2.refresh: recomputed at every ingestion by the stage regen_v2 (per-drive cache; only new or invalidated drives are re-extracted)
disclosures: integration (M475, extractor regen-v2.3): the charge integral and the speed-bin split are exact piecewise integrals of the logged channels (linear interpolation between native samples; pieces are cut at every native current and voltage sample time and every 10 km/h speed crossing); before regen-v2.3 they were a trapezoid on slices of at most 0.05 s. The run-once study blocks were produced with the slice quadrature (extractor regen-v2.1, numerically identical to regen-v2.2) and stay carried unchanged, so a difference between a carried study cell and a live cell includes this quadrature change (supported cells shift by at most 0.09 percentage points, see analyses/M475_cells.json)

exclusion reasons are first-match in the order speedGap, rpmUnknown, engineOn, currentOrVoltageUnsupported, notDecelOrFlat: per-reason counts depend on that order, the kept intervals, KE and charge do not
the estimator excludes the trimmed leading and trailing plateau intervals (their charge is reported per cohort as withTrimmedPlateaus, with the ratio when they are included)
cells above 100 % are flagged (flagAbove100) and never clipped; the number of drives above 100 % is reported per cohort
SOC and temperature contrasts are confounded with speed, demand, day and the cadence regime; no temperature, SOC, BMS-limit or health statement follows from these cells
engine off is the RPM <= 300 proxy; the field name eff is a label for the apparent KE recovery ratio (assumed mass), not an efficiency

the cadence-invariance study (regenCaptureV2Study) FAILED on the pre-registered rule; the observed layer is cadence-sensitive by about 1-2 pp, the order of the assumed-mass half-width; no display is bound to these cells (stage ME blocked, Director ruling M441 Rev 2.2)

stageMB_S1.note: stage MB variant VCa (RPM known + contiguous rows + ages <= 5 s + full probes + start-speed binning on the speed view) on the legacy extractor; step S1 of the bridge

legacyComparison.bridgeNote: S0 = published legacy; S1 = stage MB fixes on the legacy extractor; S2 = v2 intervals, strict drops only, end speed > 0, END-speed bins; S3 = + intervals ending at standstill; S4 = + inner plateaus (KE 0, charge kept); S5 = + instantaneous-speed binning (the v2 primary table). S2-S5 are masks over the v2 intervals; they are not a decomposition into independent effects (the steps interact) and not corrections.

regenCaptureV2H.label: apparent KE recovery at common sampling resolution (3 s grid, assumed mass); resolution-conditional; assumed masses; not a correction of the legacy values
regenCaptureV2H.reading: Levels of the v2 cells after every channel is reduced to a common 3 s grid (speed, current and voltage interpolated to the grid nodes, other channels latest sample, four grid phases averaged). The level depends on the resolution; the continuous-time recovery is not identified. Each level is shown with its day-clustered interval and assumed-mass range; the resolution bracket b is in the study block. Contrasts between adjacent bins are 'resolved' only under the rule of spec M442 Rev 1.2 (D5); otherwise 'not resolved at this resolution'.

outOfSupport.rule: 90 % quantile of the native speed, I or V sampling interval (positive intervals <= 5 s) > delta; more than 10 % of the native KE out of support blocks stage ME

regenCaptureV2H.refresh: recomputed at every ingestion by the stage regen_v2 (after the M442 confirm run exists)

deviation.reason: blind audit M442: the first confirm run applied the C3 out-of-support rule to the levels but not to contrasts, G2 and the sensitivities and used all even master days as the contrast day set; recomputed per spec C9, first output kept
deviation.what: C3 out-of-support mask applied to contrasts, G2 and the sensitivities; contrast and G2 day sets = days with data of the in-support drives (as the level cells); G2 testability reported; brackets, G1, G3, H1, H2 unchanged (read from the first output)

studyBasis.note: study basis: carried forward unchanged from the run-once study; not re-run on the current master

G2.note: pass is None when no cell is supported in both groups on the paired even days: NOT TESTABLE, which is not a pass

G3.rule: 90 % quantile of the native speed, I or V sampling interval (positive intervals <= 5 s) > delta; more than 10 % of the native KE out of support blocks stage ME

bracket.definition: max over f in {2,3} of |harmonized(native) - harmonized(decimated f)| (pp, point values) on all fast days; unsupported cells borrow the largest b of their view

sensitivities.note: levels of the same cells under the declared reductions (in-support drives, all days); a range over declared conventions, not an interval

regenCaptureV2HStudy.reading: Gates G1-G3 and the resolution bracket b of spec M442 Rev 1.2; H1 and H2 are reported and do not block. A contrast between adjacent bins is labelled resolved only if its even-day interval excludes 0, it exceeds b(A) + b(B), it has the same sign at both ends of the assumed-mass range and on even, odd and all days; contrasts are unadjusted for multiplicity. Sensitivities are ranges over declared conventions, not confidence intervals.
regenCaptureV2HStudy.refresh: on demand (a re-run of the confirm run needs a recorded deviation and a Director decision); each ingestion carries this block forward unchanged

regenCaptureV2Study.reading: Sensitivities are ranges over declared conventions, not confidence intervals. Cadence-invariance study: paired difference between the full-rate and the per-channel half-rate extraction on fast-cadence drives (days clustered); a cell fails if its interval excludes zero and the difference exceeds the half-width of its assumed-mass range.
regenCaptureV2Study.refresh: on demand: re-run tools/m441_study.py when the extractor, the gates or the polling regime change, or after about 14 calendar days of new drives; each ingestion carries this block forward unchanged
regenCaptureV2Study.verdict: failed; stage ME blocked (14 of 21 supported decision cells fail the pre-registered cadence-invariance rule; the strict-drop-only population is invariant, the plateau rule carries the residual)

sensitivities.note: sensitivity of the v2 estimate to declared conventions: I/V time shifted by +1 s / -1 s (BMS versus speed polling lag) and a 2 s ceiling on the speed interval and on the I/V bracket gap; differences are ranges over conventions, not confidence intervals

cadenceInvariance.rule: per cell: the paired difference (full minus decimated), mean of the two phases, with a day-clustered 95 % interval from the same resamples; a cell FAILS cadence invariance if the interval excludes zero AND |difference| exceeds the half-width of the cell's assumed-mass range; if any SUPPORTED cell (full-run fast subset) of a decision view (temperature all-SOC, speed all-SOC, SOC-band totals) fails, stage ME is blocked until the Director rules; other cells are reported only

plateauDiagnostic.note: paired full-minus-half-rate difference of the pooled ratio on the fast-cadence drives under three interval populations; a difference that appears only when plateau intervals are included points at the plateau / episode rule, not at the interpolation

resolutionBracket.definition: b_nat = max over f of |v2(native) - v2(decimated f)| (pp, point values), per stratum and cell. Fast-polled: f in {2, 3}, native v2 table against the pooled stack of the f phase variants (charge and kinetic energy summed over the phases before the ratio), all intervals (the M442 form). Slow-polled: f = 2 on the common-support variant (intervals eligible in both runs), mean of the two phases. Never borrowed across strata, cells or estimands; a cell without a computable difference shows no resolution bracket. A sensitivity on data already seen, never a gate.

regenDisplayV2.label: cadence-stratified native apparent battery-side KE recovery (assumed masses), resolution-conditional; fast-polled and slow-polled drives are not comparable; not a correction of the legacy values
regenDisplayV2.reading: Native v2 apparent KE recovery (ratio of sums over engine-off deceleration intervals, assumed class masses, 300 rpm engine-off proxy) for each polling stratum separately. A level depends on the logger's sampling resolution; the resolution bracket b_nat is the largest change of the cell value when the drives of the stratum are thinned (fast-polled by 2 and 3, slow-polled by 2). The day-clustered interval, the assumed-mass range, the resolution bracket and the plateau convention range are separate and are never combined. The two strata differ in date, season and temperature and are not contrasted; the fast-versus-slow comparison of M442 (G2) is not testable and the paired-cadence protocol PCL-1 was not run. Observed uses the actual SOC mix; SOC-standardized uses one common reference mix over the stated common-support bands and adjusts for SOC composition only.
disclosures: engine off is the RPM <= 300 proxy; assumed class masses; the field name eff is a label for the apparent KE recovery ratio, not an efficiency
temperature, SOC, speed, demand, day, season and the polling stratum are confounded in the logged data; all values are unadjusted and descriptive
the cadence-invariance study B6 FAILED for the fast-polled stratum; the M442 gate G2 is not testable; PCL-1 was not run
the 0-10 km/h and >= 130 km/h speed bins are in the payload only (payloadOnly)

regenLegacySensitivity.label: raw/ = sha256-verified originals (M366); range over declared extraction conventions; apparent KE recovery with assumed masses; not a correction of the legacy values

reproduction.note: every published temperature and speed bin (n and eff) is reproduced exactly by the study's extractor before any variant is read

regenLegacySensitivity.reading: Sensitivity of the legacy apparent KE recovery (assumed masses) to the extraction rule: each variant changes one declared rule and is compared with the legacy bar on the same drives. Delta is a range over declared conventions, not a confidence interval and not a correction of the legacy values; a nonzero Delta does not show which rule is closer to the truth. A defect is 'material' if |Delta| exceeds the half-width of the bin's published mass-uncertainty range and its 95 % day-clustered interval excludes zero in at least one valid legacy bin; 'notMaterial' is not evidence of harmlessness.
regenLegacySensitivity.refresh: on demand: re-run when the extractor, the gates or the polling regime change, or after about 14 calendar days of new drives; each ingestion carries this block forward unchanged

regenSocStandardized.label: SOC-standardized apparent KE recovery (assumed mass), standardized to the all-cohort reference SOC mix over the common-support bands; payload only
regenSocStandardized.reading: SOC-standardized apparent KE recovery (assumed mass): each bar is the KE-weighted combination over the common-support SOC bands of the joint-cell recoveries, standardized to the all-cohort reference SOC mix; it adjusts for the SOC composition of the groups only. It is not adjusted for speed, demand, season, day or the polling cadence regime (pooled bars are cadence-mixed: see the fast-polled KE share of each bar), it is not an effect of temperature and not an efficiency. A group without support in every retained SOC band is shown as unsupported for the comparison, never imputed. The intervals are conditional on the reference weights and the retained bands.
regenSocStandardized.speedViewPopulation: The speed view uses intervals with a valid SOC at the interval start (a valid pack temperature is not required); the reference weights come from intervals with a valid pack temperature and a valid SOC; the speed view is restricted to 10-70 km/h in the retained groups (spec M444 Rev 2.2 S9).

SocLevelSensitivityChart.statisticalUnit: dodSocLevelSensitivity | damage share by mean cycle-SoC band

all.basis: M91. Diagnostic SoC-window-level split of the existing rf_damage_k2 (M17) total, re-blended through a labeled, unverified weight ladder cross-checked against Wikner (Chalmers, 2017). Never folds into rf_damage_k2 itself or any GTC/FCE crossing.
all.note: At the corpus's observed band split, the weight ladder collapses to an almost class-blind multiplier on w_hi (essentially all classes already sit in the >= 50% band) -- the scenario-level ratioVsFlat and the class ranking are correspondingly close to flat. This chart is a labeled scenario ladder (weight sets applied to the fixed rf_damage_k2 SoC-band split; weights unverified, Wikner 2017 cross-check), not a sampled statistic: its uncertainty is dominated by the weight assumption, which the ladder rungs display explicitly, and the band shares are a deterministic partition of corpus damage. ThermalWarmupLag.statisticalUnit: cold-start (coolant<60C) coolant/oil warm-up: time-to-threshold, coolant-oil lag (day-clustered bootstrap), steady-state offset, paired time-domain curves

all.methodology: Cold-start drives (coolant start <60 C). Per drive on a 1 Hz grid: time from start for coolant and oil to cross 60/70/80 C; the coolant->oil lag = oil_t70 - coolant_t70; the steady-state offset = median(coolant - oil) once coolant>=80 C; and the paired warm-up curves (median temp by time-from-start bin). Medians/IQR over cold-start drives; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on the lag. Extends warmupCurve (distance-domain coolant only) with the oil trajectory and the coolant-oil lag. A possible reading of the lag is the larger thermal mass of the oil and its indirect heating; this is not tested here. Curve bins are [a, b) in seconds; samples from 900 s on are not binned (M623). A drive needs at least 30 valid 1 s coolant samples to count; the 1 s grid is on wall-clock seconds of the logged time stamps and t is seconds since the first grid second. Per bin the curve is the median across drives of the per-drive medians; p25/p75 are the spread of those per-drive medians across drives (not a confidence interval); a bin counts as supported at >= 10 drives on >= 5 calendar days; later bins hold only drives that ran that long, so part of the shape of the curve is bin composition (M624). Fuel penalty (Aug-only subset) and emissions are NOT computed here. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive.

all.basis: M63. Corpus-level pack-terminal energy accounting over the ens_outlier_v2-clean drives carrying the BMS current channel. The operating-state charge partition is the M12 torque-verified four-way partition and is exhaustive by construction.

chargeSources.label: Engine-on / non-braking charge
chargeSources.detail: engine ON, motor not braking (target torque >= -15 N·m) — engine contribution likely, but the pack shunt does not meter generator output

chargeSources.label: Engine-on / braking overlap
chargeSources.detail: engine ON while the motor brakes — mixed operating state; the physical split between generator output and recovered braking energy is unidentified

chargeSources.label: Engine-off / braking charge
chargeSources.detail: engine OFF, motor braking — strongest regenerative-braking-at-pack proxy, conditional on the torque/RPM state classification

chargeSources.label: Engine-off residual charge
chargeSources.detail: engine OFF, motor not braking — unattributed by the -15 N·m threshold; not a metered motor or generator source

unobservable.why: the BMS shunt only sees current crossing the pack terminals; bus-direct energy never appears in any logged channel, so the direct/buffered split cannot be derived from this data at any sample rate

unobservable.quantity: engine brake thermal efficiency / fuel energy in

each needs input and output power at the same node simultaneously; only one side of each node is instrumented

ThermalFuelPenalty.statisticalUnit: cold-start (coolant<60C) fuel-accumulator association: trip-level naive ratio, matched-operating-point fuel-rate association, matched-speed duty-cycle, idle L/hr, continuous coolant/oil-temperature covariate model

tripLevel.note: Confounded: warm-up window is early/low-speed/urban (regime) and can bank fuel to the pack (SoC drift median disclosed). See combustionPenalty and dutyCycle for the regime/operating-point-controlled decomposition.

combustionPenalty.note: Fuel burned per engine-on second at a matched RPM x load operating point, cold vs warm; exposure-weighted by warm-state cell counts (realistic mix). A conditional contrast at matched RPM x load; enrichment, cold friction, oil and coolant state and demand stay entangled, so it is not attributed to one mechanism. Coarse bins; the effect rests largely on the most-populated cell.

dutyCycle.note: Engine-on fraction (rpm>400) at matched road speed, cold vs warm: a descriptive conditional contrast. The series-hybrid runs the ICE more when cold; catalyst light-off, cold charge/idle strategy, coolant and oil state and demand stay entangled, so it is not attributed to one mechanism.

all.methodology: Fuel-accumulator subset (2026-08-12 to 2026-11-09, 66 days, 167 cold-start drives; Module H fuel channel). Cold-start drives: coolant start <60 C reaching >=70 C, carrying the used-fuel accumulator. 1 Hz grid (generous ffill for the ~0.25 Hz coolant multiplex group). Four views: (1) tripLevel naive warm-up-window vs warm-window L/100km (regime- and SoC-confounded, disclosed); (2) combustionPenalty = fuel per engine-on second at matched RPMxload (a conditional contrast at matched RPMxload; enrichment, cold friction, oil and coolant state and demand stay entangled; day-clustered bootstrap, seed 42, 4000 draws); (3) dutyCycle = engine-on fraction at matched road speed (a conditional duty contrast at matched road speed; strategy, coolant, oil and catalyst state and demand stay entangled; the larger of the two contrasts); (4) idle fuel/hour at standstill. SUBSET CAVEATS: warm-season only (mild cold-start, coolant starts ~ambient, NOT winter), urban-dominated. Emissions NOT instrumented; no generator-efficiency/CAP used. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive.

continuousCovariateModel.method: Day-clustered bootstrap OLS (_dayboot_ols, the SAME estimator M223.1 introduced, reused directly), continuous coolant (and oil, where available) temperature plus RPM/load controls -- replaces the binary coldStartMaxC/warmThresholdC step function with an actual continuous relationship. A negative coolant/oil coefficient means fuel rate keeps falling smoothly as the engine warms, not just stepping down at one threshold. coolantCiSpansZero=true means the continuous coolant effect is NOT resolved once RPM/load are controlled for at this sample size (not resolved; an absence of detection, not evidence of no effect) -- this does not contradict combustionPenalty's own resolved BINARY warmup-vs-warm ratio above, since that comparison pools cells differently and this model estimates a single linear slope across the full continuous range rather than a coarse two-state contrast; both are reported, neither is suppressed to make the other look cleaner.

withinDayMatchedSubset.note: 51 of 66 days in the cold-start subset have >=2 qualifying drives (152 drives total) -- a within-day comparison would partially control for weather/route, but the eligible subset is too small for a separate fit at this corpus size; reported honestly rather than fit anyway.

EvTraction.statisticalUnit: M53 pure-electric (engine-off) traction census: engine-off distance share by drive type, max EV run, buffer-limit cross-check

caveats: EV state is eng_rpm <= 400 (engine not rotating), the same threshold engine_on_pct uses. The M46/M48 motored-unfuelled state counts here as engine ON (it is not engine-off by RPM), so these figures are a conservative reading of "electric"; the comparison with a zero-logged-fuel definition on the fuel-instrumented drives is evTraction.zeroFuelVariant.

The +/-3 s nearest-sample channel alignment and the symmetric 3 s state debounce can move the engine-off boundaries in either direction (an engine-on run shorter than 3 s inside an engine-off run is absorbed, which raises the EV share; an engine-off run shorter than 3 s inside an engine-on run is absorbed, which lowers it): every EV distance and time figure is an estimated RPM-defined engine-off share, not a one-sided bound. Detector settings (threshold, sample age, debounce, alignment) give a sensitivity range, not a confidence interval; unknown RPM is never counted as engine-off (M427, audit F04).
Runs at the top of the distribution recover 30-50% of throughput as regen mid-run, so the observed maximum is not a buffer-drain range; runMaxUnassistedKm is.

M62: the census rests on nValid of nDrives (supportPct); the balance is channel-gated. Drives whose ensemble outlier flags were never fitted (NaN) are treated as non-outliers and INCLUDED -- see nUnflaggedIncluded / kmUnflaggedIncluded for how much distance that assumption admits.
The barometric PID is 1 kPa (~83 m) quantised and cannot resolve run-scale gradient, so no terrain attribution is made for long runs.

HighSocRegen.statisticalUnit: high-SoC charge-power envelope by SoC bin (p95 bootstrap), demand-controlled (pure-regen-only) subset, engine-on/non-decelerating composition disclosure

all.populationCaveat: M231 (audit F06): this envelope's population is charge power in (1, 120) kW while SoC is valid -- it is NOT restricted to regenerative braking. Of these samples, 68.2% are engine-on (generator charging, not necessarily regen) and 61.4% are non-decelerating (charging while steady or accelerating -- engine-on generator charging can do this). See demandControlledRegen for a subset restricted to samples that cannot plausibly be anything other than regenerative braking.

demandControlledRegen.methodology: Restricted to rpm<=300 (engine off/idle) & speed>3 km/h & instantaneous deceleration (speed[t-1]-speed[t])>0 & target motor torque<0 (motor braking, not propulsion) -- a demand-controlled subset that cannot plausibly be anything other than regenerative braking, unlike the unfiltered charging-power population above. Same SoC bins, same day-clustered-bootstrap protocol (seed 44/45, 4000 draws), and the SAME median-of-high-bins-p95 statistic paired correctly with its own bootstrap CI.

all.interpretation: The high-SoC CHARGING-POWER p95 envelope (NOT exclusively regen -- see populationCaveat) is dome-shaped: it rises from low SoC, peaks mid-band, then declines mildly toward the top -- a modest high-SoC charge-acceptance taper, not a hard cutoff. THIN effect, confounded by the driving distribution across SoC; reported descriptively. demandControlledRegen (restricted to samples that cannot plausibly be anything other than regenerative braking) shows the same qualitative taper.
all.methodology: Charging-power samples (M231: renamed from "regen samples" -- see populationCaveat) = charge power I*V/1000 kW in (1, 120) kW (cap drops sensor glitches). Envelope = median/p95/p99 charge kW per SoC bin (bins need >=50 samples). High-SoC reduction = drop in p95 from the peak bin to the MEDIAN (not mean) of bins at SoC>=69%. Day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42/43, 4000 draws) on the peak-bin p95 (peakBinP95Boot), the single top-SoC-bin p95 (topBinP95Boot), and -- M231 fix for the estimand mismatch -- the SAME median-of-high-bins statistic as highSocP95Kw itself (highSocP95Boot), so the reported point estimate and its CI are always the same aggregate. The p95/p99 envelope (not the mean) is used because charge-power magnitude is set by demand intensity, not SoC -- the envelope is the observed ceiling, not an identified BMS acceptance limit. THIN per the feasibility review. Single vehicle / ~single driver.
all.covariateMethodology: M226.2 (P1.2, enhancement plan): the SAME regen-sample definition as highSocRegen (charge power in (1, 120) kW), stratified jointly by SoC bin (highSocRegen's own edges) and a deceleration-intensity tercile (instantaneous speed[t-1]-speed[t], km/h per 1 s sample -- the same per-sample granularity regenByZone's own raw pass uses, deliberately reused rather than a new multi-second event definition). p90/p95/p99 reported per joint cell (quantile stratification, not a fitted quantile-regression/GAM model -- this codebase's established binned-not-parametric convention). declineSurvivesAdjustment is TRUE only if the high-SoC (>=69%) p95 decline vs. the peak-p95 SoC bin holds in EVERY decel-intensity stratum; declineByStratum reports the actual per-stratum comparison so this is checkable, not just asserted. A genuine open question per the plan -- reported honestly either way.

cold.interpretation: The high-SoC CHARGING-POWER p95 envelope (NOT exclusively regen -- see populationCaveat) is dome-shaped: it rises from low SoC, peaks mid-band, then declines mildly toward the top -- a modest high-SoC charge-acceptance taper, not a hard cutoff. THIN effect, confounded by the driving distribution across SoC; reported descriptively. demandControlledRegen (restricted to samples that cannot plausibly be anything other than regenerative braking) shows the same qualitative taper.
cold.methodology: Charging-power samples (M231: renamed from "regen samples" -- see populationCaveat) = charge power I*V/1000 kW in (1, 120) kW (cap drops sensor glitches). Envelope = median/p95/p99 charge kW per SoC bin (bins need >=50 samples). High-SoC reduction = drop in p95 from the peak bin to the MEDIAN (not mean) of bins at SoC>=69%. Day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42/43, 4000 draws) on the peak-bin p95 (peakBinP95Boot), the single top-SoC-bin p95 (topBinP95Boot), and -- M231 fix for the estimand mismatch -- the SAME median-of-high-bins statistic as highSocP95Kw itself (highSocP95Boot), so the reported point estimate and its CI are always the same aggregate. The p95/p99 envelope (not the mean) is used because charge-power magnitude is set by demand intensity, not SoC -- the envelope is the observed ceiling, not an identified BMS acceptance limit. THIN per the feasibility review. Single vehicle / ~single driver.
cold.covariateMethodology: M226.2 (P1.2, enhancement plan): the SAME regen-sample definition as highSocRegen (charge power in (1, 120) kW), stratified jointly by SoC bin (highSocRegen's own edges) and a deceleration-intensity tercile (instantaneous speed[t-1]-speed[t], km/h per 1 s sample -- the same per-sample granularity regenByZone's own raw pass uses, deliberately reused rather than a new multi-second event definition). p90/p95/p99 reported per joint cell (quantile stratification, not a fitted quantile-regression/GAM model -- this codebase's established binned-not-parametric convention). declineSurvivesAdjustment is TRUE only if the high-SoC (>=69%) p95 decline vs. the peak-p95 SoC bin holds in EVERY decel-intensity stratum; declineByStratum reports the actual per-stratum comparison so this is checkable, not just asserted. A genuine open question per the plan -- reported honestly either way.

BufferDebtRecovery.statisticalUnit: engine-start buffer-debt recovery: per-event discharge-debt integration, recovery half-time, fixed-checkpoint (10/30/60/120s) repayment fractions, day-clustered bootstrap

all.methodology: Extends M116: reuses _buffer_impulse_events verbatim for the engine-start discharge-impulse set and its per-event energy debt (>= 3 Wh). On a 1 Hz I/V grid, integrates net-discharge Wh from the event over a 120 s recovery window (signed p=(-I)*V, M11). The debt peak is the cumulative-net-discharge maximum (~impulse end); recovery is measured from there. recoveryHalfTimeS = time to repay 50 % of the debt; fracRecovered120 = net fraction repaid by window end (clamped <=1); overshootFrac = peak refill PAST the debt (generator banking buffer headroom while running); fracNotRecovered120 = residual; socRecoveredPP is the independent SoC cross-check. M221.2: frac10S/30S/60S sample the SAME cumulative recovery curve at three more fixed post-peak checkpoints (10/30/60s), each with its own overshoot rate (recovered > 1.0, unclamped, at that specific checkpoint) -- checkpoints beyond the recovery window edge are excluded, not fabricated. Per-event medians/IQR; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on median half-time. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive.

HandoffSequence.statisticalUnit: engine-start battery/engine/turbo handoff sequence: coarse lag (discharge peak, load-point, boost onset, discharge relax) vs start, modal event ordering, day-clustered bootstrap

all.methodology: Handoff = canonical engine start (_engine_start_triggers, reused from M116). Around each start t0, coarse event times on a 1 Hz grid: battery-discharge peak (argmax of p=(-I)*V over [t0-8,t0+30]); load-point reached (first rpm>=1400 at/after t0); boost onset (first boost>=0.10 bar); discharge relaxation (first drop below half the discharge peak after the peak). Per-event coarse lag vs t0 (median/IQR) and the modal event ORDERING are reported; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on the load-point and boost-onset lags. Extends M116 (start) and M118 (ramp latency) with the full battery/engine/turbo sequence. COARSE ONLY: ordering resolvable to ~+/-1-2 s; t10/t50/t90 are below the logged-cadence floor and are NOT reported. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive.

EngineStartContext.statisticalUnit: engine-start context taxonomy: pre-start SoC/discharge/torque-demand/coolant classification (lowBuffer/socMaintenance/highDemand/highSpeedCruise/creepLaunch/coldEngine), threshold sensitivity sweep, day-clustered bootstrap

all.methodology: Canonical engine-start trigger (_engine_start_triggers: RPM>800 preceded by sustained RPM<=100 for >=3 s -- the same debounced detector M116/M119 use, NOT the frozen M119-v2 hazard model). For each start, pre-start context is read from a 1 Hz grid: SoC/speed/coolant at the last valid sample in [t0-2s, t0]; demand = median discharge kW and median clipped TARGET torque over [t0-5s, t0-1s] (M102: actual torque invalid). Multi-label rules (thresholds grounded on the observed pre-start distributions, sweep shipped): lowBuffer SoC<=55; socMaintenance 55<SoC<=63; highDemand disc>=20 kW or tqTgt>=60 N.m; highSpeedCruise speed>=70; creepLaunch speed<20; coldEngine coolant<=60 C. Labels are multi (a start may carry several); starts matching no rule are reported as unclassified, not forced. Day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on per-drive starts/100 km. Formal hand-validation against a user-labelled subset is pending -- an illustrative classified sample is shipped for it. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive.

CellSpreadRelaxation.statisticalUnit: exploratory max-min cell-voltage spread relaxation on >=5s rest windows following a loaded period: loaded spread, rest asymptote, relaxation magnitude/half-time, day-clustered bootstrap

all.interpretation: Exploratory. Over 865 rest windows (652 drives, 117 days) the median logged max-min cell spread is 11 mV at load-off (IQR 9-13.5) and 10 mV at rest (IQR 8-12). The median relaxation magnitude is 1 mV (day-clustered 95% CI 1 to 1.5), at the 1 mV step of the logged spread; the relaxation time is not resolvable at the logged cadence. Max and Min are BMS-reported channels polled in a cycle; this is not a cell balance, health or stress diagnosis.
all.methodology: Rest window = |I|<5 A sustained >=5 s, immediately preceded by a loaded period (mean |I|>=20 A over the prior 3 s). Per window: spread (max-min)*1000 mV at load-off, the rest asymptote (median of the last up-to-5 s), the relaxation magnitude (onset-asymptote) and the half-time (first second below onset-0.5*magnitude, only for >1 mV relaxations). Median/IQR over rest windows; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on the magnitude. EXPLORATORY; no cell diagnosis; sub-5 s relaxation is not resolvable at this cadence. Distinct from cellHealthTrend (long-term unloaded level). Single vehicle / ~single driver.

Boundary-vs-mid reported as within-drive paired deltas (drive is its own control). Boundary windows are low-speed by construction, which confounds engine-on/battery-kW; for those a SPEED-MATCHED control uses mid-third seconds within the boundary window speed band [p10,p90]. SoC and coolant are not speed-driven, so their departure deltas are the confound-free headlines (day-clustered bootstrap, seed 42, 4000 draws). Time-normalised (GPS-free, corpus-wide). Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive.

RpmSpeedSync.statisticalUnit: engine-on RPM vs wheel-speed synchronization: per-drive Spearman rho + OLS slope + load-point fraction, pooled RPM-by-speed-bin envelope, lead/lag cross-correlation, day-clustered bootstrap

leadLagExploratory.note: Per-drive best speed-RPM cross-correlation lag over ±2 s. At the logged cadence this is near the resolvable floor -- exploratory/descriptive only, no timing claim.

all.methodology: Engine RPM vs wheel speed over engine-on (rpm>400) moving (speed>=3.0 km/h) 1 Hz samples, per drive. Spearman rho (rank monotonicity), OLS slope (rpm per km/h) and load-point fraction (rpm in [1975,2025]) summarised as per-drive median/IQR; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) on median rho. rpmBySpeed is the pooled engine-on RPM occupancy envelope per speed bin. Contrast: a fixed-ratio geartrain gives rho~1 and a steep gear-stepped slope; the low rho and shallow slope here quantify the series-hybrid decoupling (engine serves the generator/buffer, not the wheels). Lead/lag is exploratory (cadence-limited). No acoustic/NVH claim -- no cabin-noise channel exists. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive.

EnergyShifting.statisticalUnit: exploratory energy-shifting behaviour: engine-on fraction and net battery power by vehicle speed bin, no acoustic claim

all.methodology: Per-drive 1 Hz grid (speed via M167 priority). Per speed bin: engine-on fraction (rpm>400), summarised as per-drive median/IQR with a day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) at low speed; and pooled median NET battery power p=(-I)*V (M11, discharge-positive). The energy-shifting signature is net discharge at low speed (buffer supplying electric operation, engine off) and net charge where the engine runs with headroom (banking generator energy). NO acoustic / quietness claim -- there is no microphone; whether the shifting is noise-, efficiency- or demand-motivated is NOT identifiable. Exploratory. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive.

VgtAirPath.statisticalUnit: VGT-A commanded-vs-actual position tracking error (engine-on only) + air-path operating map (VGT position vs boost/RPM/MAF/AFR), day-clustered bootstrap

EngineStateMachine.statisticalUnit: engine operating-point state machine: RPM-band (off/low/loadPoint/mid/high) occupancy, dwell, first-order transition matrix, per-state battery power

all.methodology: Per-second engine operating-point state on a 1 Hz grid: off rpm<400; low 400-1400; loadPoint 1400-2300 (the OEM-nominal ~2000-rpm generator load-point -- NOT a measured BSFC optimum, no efficiency claim); mid 2300-3200; high >=3200. Per drive: state occupancy, within-drive first-order transition counts (t->t+1), per-state dwell run-lengths, per-state entry counts and per-state battery kW (p=(-I)*V, M11). Occupancy is per-drive median/IQR with a day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws); occupancy.<state>.pooled (M203) is the corpus-pooled, duration-weighted share of ALL classified engine time -- derived from the transition-matrix row sums, so it excludes only the single last classified sample of each drive (~0.05% relative undercount at this corpus size). Use pooled for "how much of engine time", not the per-drive median: mid/high are zero-inflated across drives (most individual drives never reach the state at all), so their per-drive median reads 0% even though pooled occupancy is real and non-trivial; "off" per-drive median reads above pooled because short/idle-heavy drives skew the median upward. Pooled "off" matches rpmDistribution.pooledPct[0] and evTraction.evPctTime (independent pooled computations over the same classified seconds). Dwell, entry rate (per engine-on hour), battery kW and the transition matrix are pooled. Extends rpmDistribution (occupancy only) and M118 (start-dwell only) with the full dwell/entry/transition state machine. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive.

AccelDecelEnvelopes.statisticalUnit: accel/decel speed-binned dynamics envelopes: battery power/RPM/boost/SoC-rate/target-torque by speed bin and phase, jerk, threshold sensitivity, day-clustered bootstrap

jerkExploratory.note: Jerk = |d(accel_g)/dt| on the native logged-cadence grid; noisy and cadence-limited. Descriptive/exploratory only (candidate P), NOT a headline.

all.methodology: Per-drive 1 Hz grid (resample -> ffill(limit=3); speed resolved by the M167 VCM/OBD priority rule). Phase from the LOGGED accel(g) sensor (schema-v6 slim cache, native logged cadence, NOT diff(speed)): ACCEL accg>=+0.020 g, DECEL accg<=-0.020 g, moving samples (speed>=3.0 km/h) only. Battery power p=(-I)*V/1000 kW (M11 discharge-positive): +ve = traction draw, -ve = regen/charge. Speed-binned median/IQR of accg, battKw, engine RPM, boost, per-second SoC-rate and TARGET motor torque (M102: actual torque/RPM invalid, target is the command signal). Aggregation is drive/day (never 1 Hz seconds as replicates for CIs); pooled sample median/IQR for the per-bin envelope shape (nSamples), day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) over per-drive medians for the headline battKw CIs. thresholdSensitivity sweeps the accel/decel threshold. Sub-second latency/time-constants are below the cadence floor and NOT reported; jerk is exploratory only; per-second SoC-rate is SoC-quantisation-dominated (0.5 % steps) and carried only for completeness. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive, no control-strategy or population claim.

CrawlStopGo.statisticalUnit: crawl and stop-go operating-mode census: launch/approach/cycle buffer energy, recovery ratio, starts per 10min stop-go, zero-inflation two-part regen/restart-probability model, day-clustered bootstrap

all.rateCaveat: startsPer10minStopGo = startsLowSpeed / (lowSpeedTimeS/600), computed per drive then aggregated by drive type. The denominator (seconds at <=stopGoCeil km/h) is NOT a fixed window -- it is whatever low-speed time that one drive actually contains. Urban drives spend the majority of their duration in this band (large, stable denominator); drive types in smallDenominatorDriveTypes (median low-speed time <20% of drive duration -- typically highway/mixed_highway) touch it only in brief, episodic windows: ramps, toll gates, a congestion pinch-point, not a sustained stop-go duty cycle. A handful of discrete engine starts landing inside a short low-speed window inflates the ratio; the identical window with zero starts reads zero -- hence the wide IQR/p95 on these types relative to urban. Read the rate together with lowSpeedTimeS (the window size) and startsLowSpeedAbs (the raw count) reported alongside it, not in isolation. This is the same short-window/small-sample denominator pattern already documented corpus-wide for short-trip throughput (M35), here affecting a rate rather than an intensity figure. Descriptive only: no claim that highway driving produces more frequent stop-go engine cycling in absolute terms -- the opposite is true (urban carries far more absolute low-speed/engine-start volume); this is purely about per-drive-type rate variance from a small, uneven denominator.
all.methodology: Per-drive 1 Hz grid. STOP = speed<1.5 km/h sustained >=3 s; LAUNCH/APPROACH = transient to/from 15 km/h (cap 20 s); STOP-GO CYCLE = consecutive-stop pair with inter-stop speed peak <=30 km/h. Energy p_dis=(-I)*V/1000 kW (M11 discharge-positive): whCycleNet = signed integral over the cycle; whLaunchOut / whApproachIn = gross discharge-out / regen-in over the phase windows; recoveryRatio = in/out. Aggregation is cycle/drive/day (never 1 Hz seconds as replicates); medians/IQR for skewed energy; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) for headline CIs. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive characterisation, no control-strategy or population claim. Sub-second launch dynamics (jerk, t10/t50/t90) are below the logged-cadence floor and are NOT reported. Speed is the VCM/OBD channel, not wheel-speed; thresholdSensitivity sweeps the STOP_V and stop-go-ceiling cuts so the headline does not hinge on one threshold. byDriveType covers every drive of that type passing the >=120-sample speed-data gate (n sums to nDrivesCovered), including drives with zero stop-go activity -- it is not filtered to drives where a cycle was detected. M204 (2026-09-01) added lowSpeedTimeS / lowSpeedFracOfDrive / startsLowSpeedAbs to byDriveType and out.rateCaveat, since startsPer10minStopGo divides a small numerator by a per-drive-type-uneven denominator and reads misleadingly on its own for episodic-low-speed drive types; see out.rateCaveat for the full interpretation.

movingSegmentComparison.note: New segment-extraction sub-pass (continuously-moving runs, speed never below 1.5 km/h for >=20s, same 1 Hz grid _csg_grid already builds) -- not individually matched pair-by-pair on mean speed; the two populations' overall speed and net-energy distributions are reported side by side instead, since strict per-cycle matching at this sample size would leave very few matched pairs. A coarser but disclosed comparison, not silently narrowed. MEDIAN SPEED GAP: 23.2 km/h (moving) vs. 6.0 km/h (cycles, peak) -- the two populations are NOT speed-matched at this sample size, disclosed numerically rather than only in prose; treat the net-energy comparison as two different operating regimes shown side by side, not a matched-pair contrast.

all.twoPartMethodology: M226.1 (P1.1, enhancement plan): two-part model over the SAME approach/cycle event lists crawlStopGo itself builds. Part 1 (regenProbability): empirical P(grossInWh>0), day-clustered bootstrap CI (seed=42, 4000 draws), not a fitted parametric logistic. Part 2 (conditionalMagnitude): quantiles of grossInWh GIVEN grossInWh>0 -- crawlStopGo.whPerApproachRegen/recoveryRatio (pooled, including zeros) are retained unchanged for continuity. netCycleByPeakSpeed bins whCycleNet by peak-speed x deceleration-intensity tercile (decel rate = peak speed / approach-phase duration, the same window crawlStopGo's own energy phases already use). restartProbability/stopEffectCovariates use the SAME day-clustered-bootstrap-proportion estimator throughout. movingSegmentComparison is the one new segment-extraction sub-pass (see its own note) -- everything else re-derives _csg_grid/_csg_events (frame_loader-cached, not a new raw pass) rather than touching crawlStopGo itself, so crawlStopGo's existing fields are unaffected by construction. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive, not causal.

windows.label: Launch
windows.mask: stop end to the first sample at or above min(15 km/h, inter-stop peak); not capped at 20 s

windows.label: Creep
windows.mask: samples strictly between the launch window end and the approach window start; empty (excluded, not zero) when the two windows are adjacent or share a sample

windows.label: Approach
windows.mask: last sample at or above min(15 km/h, inter-stop peak) to the start of the next stop; not capped at 20 s

windows.label: Full cycle
windows.mask: end of one stop to the start of the next stop (consecutive-stop pair, inter-stop peak <= 30 km/h)

phaseEnergy.methodology: M356 (Cs-21). Energy over each window of the stop-go cycle from logged HV current x voltage on the 1 Hz grid (asynchronous polling; samples with no I*V are dropped, so energy over gaps is understated; gridCoverageMedian is the non-NaN share). net = signed sum; discharge-direction and regen-direction (positive magnitude) are the sums of the positive and negative parts of the power. The windows are NOT additive: launch and approach share one boundary sample when launch end = approach start, and the creep window is empty (excluded, not zero) in that case; additiveShare is the share of cycles with launch end < approach start. One-direction energies are biased upward by sign-flipping noise (rectification); the net is not. Zero = value <= 0; where the zero share is >= 0.25 the two-part form is reported (day-clustered P(>0) and the positive-part median with CI). Day-clustered percentile bootstrap, seed 42, 4000 draws. Reconstructed from logged data, never measured energy. raw/ = sha256-verified originals (M366): zero shares are slightly lower than on the former lower-precision re-exports, which carried integer-rounded current (M365 comparison).

shoulder.rateCaveat: startsPer10minStopGo = startsLowSpeed / (lowSpeedTimeS/600), computed per drive then aggregated by drive type. The denominator (seconds at <=stopGoCeil km/h) is NOT a fixed window -- it is whatever low-speed time that one drive actually contains. Urban drives spend the majority of their duration in this band (large, stable denominator); drive types in smallDenominatorDriveTypes (median low-speed time <20% of drive duration -- typically highway/mixed_highway) touch it only in brief, episodic windows: ramps, toll gates, a congestion pinch-point, not a sustained stop-go duty cycle. A handful of discrete engine starts landing inside a short low-speed window inflates the ratio; the identical window with zero starts reads zero -- hence the wide IQR/p95 on these types relative to urban. Read the rate together with lowSpeedTimeS (the window size) and startsLowSpeedAbs (the raw count) reported alongside it, not in isolation. This is the same short-window/small-sample denominator pattern already documented corpus-wide for short-trip throughput (M35), here affecting a rate rather than an intensity figure. Descriptive only: no claim that highway driving produces more frequent stop-go engine cycling in absolute terms -- the opposite is true (urban carries far more absolute low-speed/engine-start volume); this is purely about per-drive-type rate variance from a small, uneven denominator.
shoulder.methodology: Per-drive 1 Hz grid. STOP = speed<1.5 km/h sustained >=3 s; LAUNCH/APPROACH = transient to/from 15 km/h (cap 20 s); STOP-GO CYCLE = consecutive-stop pair with inter-stop speed peak <=30 km/h. Energy p_dis=(-I)*V/1000 kW (M11 discharge-positive): whCycleNet = signed integral over the cycle; whLaunchOut / whApproachIn = gross discharge-out / regen-in over the phase windows; recoveryRatio = in/out. Aggregation is cycle/drive/day (never 1 Hz seconds as replicates); medians/IQR for skewed energy; day-clustered bootstrap (seed 42, 4000 draws) for headline CIs. Single vehicle / ~single driver -- descriptive characterisation, no control-strategy or population claim. Sub-second launch dynamics (jerk, t10/t50/t90) are below the logged-cadence floor and are NOT reported. Speed is the VCM/OBD channel, not wheel-speed; thresholdSensitivity sweeps the STOP_V and stop-go-ceiling cuts so the headline does not hinge on one threshold. byDriveType covers every drive of that type passing the >=120-sample speed-data gate (n sums to nDrivesCovered), including drives with zero stop-go activity -- it is not filtered to drives where a cycle was detected. M204 (2026-09-01) added lowSpeedTimeS / lowSpeedFracOfDrive / startsLowSpeedAbs to byDriveType and out.rateCaveat, since startsPer10minStopGo divides a small numerator by a per-drive-type-uneven denominator and reads misleadingly on its own for episodic-low-speed drive types; see out.rateCaveat for the full interpretation.

movingSegmentComparison.note: New segment-extraction sub-pass (continuously-moving runs, speed never below 1.5 km/h for >=20s, same 1 Hz grid _csg_grid already builds) -- not individually matched pair-by-pair on mean speed; the two populations' overall speed and net-energy distributions are reported side by side instead, since strict per-cycle matching at this sample size would leave very few matched pairs. A coarser but disclosed comparison, not silently narrowed. MEDIAN SPEED GAP: 22.1 km/h (moving) vs. 5.0 km/h (cycles, peak) -- the two populations are NOT speed-matched at this sample size, disclosed numerically rather than only in prose; treat the net-energy comparison as two different operating regimes shown side by side, not a matched-pair contrast.

shoulder.twoPartMethodology: M226.1 (P1.1, enhancement plan): two-part model over the SAME approach/cycle event lists crawlStopGo itself builds. thermalSupportLedger.cohortNote: warm, shoulder and cold reproduce the cohort variants of the thermal charts (seasonal_drive_master thermal_regime); the cold cohort (55 drives, 11 days) meets the minimum support
censoringReading: a drive that does not reach a threshold is a right-censored observation: its observation ended (key-off) before the threshold

the pooled time-to-threshold medians of thermalWarmupLag are medians of the reachers only; censored drives are excluded, so the median understates the time for all cold starts; where fewer than half of the cold starts reached the threshold the cohort median is not identifiable without an assumption on censoring

risk-set rows are counts at fixed times, not a time-to-event estimate; censoring by key-off may be informative: the Kaplan-Meier (product-limit) estimate in timeToThreshold assumes it is not, and carries worst-case identification bounds and a hazard-tilt sensitivity

winter (December to February) stays unobserved: the cold cohort (55 drives on 11 days, driver-recorded start ambient -1 to 5 C) supports a cohort view, not a winter inference; few days, so the intervals are wide
limits: single vehicle, one driver, May-November 2026, ambient -1 to 38 C (start ambient recorded for 402 of 454 cold starts)
the cold-start definitions differ by estimator on purpose (coolant <= 50 C, none, < 60 C): each ledger states its own
the ledger classifies drives with the estimator's own rules and checks its accepted counts against the published n; a changed estimator rule makes the reconciliation fail until the ledger is updated
